subject.title: RFC: allow organization publishers to set a GitHub profile independent of their handle

question: Should organization publishers receive a GitHub-specific profile override, who may edit it, and must ClawHub verify the linked GitHub organization before presenting it as verified?
rationale: The source confirms the capability is missing, but the issue leaves the durable data contract, authorization boundary, and verification semantics open; these choices affect schema, UI language, API behavior, and future trust guarantees.

options.title: Add narrow GitHub metadata
options.body: Store an optional normalized GitHub handle, allow organization owners and admins to edit it, and treat it as unverified public metadata unless separate ownership verification exists.

options.title: Require verified ownership
options.body: Add the override only after OAuth organization-membership verification can prove that an authorized ClawHub member controls the linked GitHub organization.

options.title: Use a general website field
options.body: Add a broader organization website URL instead of GitHub-specific identity, accepting that this does not provide GitHub ownership semantics.

recommendation.title: Add narrow GitHub metadata
recommendation.body: Store an optional normalized GitHub handle, allow organization owners and admins to edit it, and treat it as unverified public metadata unless separate ownership verification exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent merged work defining organization ownership behavior and its separation from personal-account state.
